issues.description: Field: orders. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) explicitly requires a modifiable List<Meal> attribute called `orders` (lines 70-71). However, the provided solution implements `orders` as a Meal[] array (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java, line 4: `private Meal[] orders;`) and the template utility ArrayHelpers (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/ArrayHelpers.java, lines 13-17) provides array-based helpers (addElementToArray/removeFirstElementFromArray). This inconsistency between the specified collection type (List) and the codebase examples/utilities (array) will confuse students about which collection to implement and which APIs/helpers to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type for `orders` consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Two viable approaches: (A) Prefer arrays: update the problem statement and UML to specify `orders` as Meal[] (or describe it as an array) and mention using the provided ArrayHelpers; adjust wording that asked for List<Meal>. (B) Prefer lists: modify the template to include List-based helpers (e.g., use ArrayList<Meal>), replace ArrayHelpers usage with List APIs, and update the solution to use List<Meal> and corresponding methods. Apply the chosen change to the UML in the problem statement and to any example code so students receive a single, unambiguous expectation.
